sec: Amiodarone Type I vs Type II & Differential Diagnosis Grid

items.q: Amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism is typically a transient phenomenon mediated by which physiological mechanism?
opts: Wolff-Chaikoff phenomenon due to massive iodine load
items.exp: Under Amiodarone induces: Hypothyroidism is a 'Transient phenomenon' 'D/t Wolff chaikoff phenomenon'. (Book p916)

items.q: Match the type of amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis to its underlying pathophysiology — 1) Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis Type-I 2) Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis Type-II … A) Patient with underlying thyroid disease (Graves or MNG); Jod-Basedow phenomenon; ↑↑ vascularity B) No underlying disease; lysosomal-mediated destruction; no antibodies; ↓↓ vascularity
items.exp: Type I occurs in underlying disease via Jod-Basedow with ↑↑ vascularity; Type II occurs without underlying disease via lysosomal destruction with ↓↓ vascularity. (Book p916)

items.q: What is the medical drug of choice (DOC) for Amiodarone-Induced Thyrotoxicosis Type I versus Type II?
opts: Type I: Thionamides (DOC); Type II: Corticosteroids (Steroids)
Type I: Corticosteroids; Type II: Thionamides
Type I: Radioactive iodine; Type II: High-dose aspirin
Type I: Lithium carbonate; Type II: Potassium iodide
items.exp: Management: Type-I -> Stop treatment, Start Thionamide (DOC); Type-II -> Drug should be stopped, Rx -> Steroid. (Book p916)

items.q: A 62-year-old man on chronic amiodarone therapy develops thyrotoxicosis. Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrates absent/markedly decreased thyroid vascularity (↓↓ vascularity), and autoantibodies are negative. What is the diagnosis and treatment?
opts: Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis Type II; stop drug and treat with steroids
Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis Type I; treat with thionamides
Graves disease; treat with radioactive iodine ablation
Subacute de Quervain thyroiditis; treat with aspirin
items.exp: Type II has no underlying disease, no antibodies, markedly decreased vascularity, and is treated by stopping amiodarone and starting steroids. (Book p916)

items.q: In the comparison table on page 916, match the condition to its typical symptom duration — 1) Subacute Thyroiditis 2) Graves' Disease 3) Toxic MNG … A) Days to weeks B) 2 - 3 months C) Months to years
items.exp: Duration: Subacute Thyroiditis lasts days to weeks; Graves' Disease lasts 2-3 months; Toxic MNG lasts months to years. (Book p916)

items.q: In which entity alone is local neck pain characteristically present in the page 916 comparison grid?
items.exp: Under Neck pain: Present in Subacute Thyroiditis; Absent in Graves' Disease; Absent in Toxic MNG. (Book p916)

items.q: Match the goiter physical characteristics on page 916 — 1) Subacute Thyroiditis 2) Graves' Disease 3) Toxic MNG … A) Small goiter B) Diffuse goiter C) Nodular goiter
items.exp: Goiter type: Subacute Thyroiditis = Small; Graves' Disease = Diffuse; Toxic MNG = Nodular. (Book p916)

items.q: Regarding extrathyroidal manifestations (ophthalmopathy and dermopathy): I Present in Graves' disease. II Absent in both Subacute thyroiditis and Toxic multinodular goiter.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Ophthalmopathy / Dermopathy is Absent in Subacute Thyroiditis, Present in Graves' Disease, and Absent in Toxic MNG. (Book p916)

items.q: In differentiating hyperthyroid conditions on page 916, the serum T3/T4 ratio is ___ in subacute thyroiditis, but ___ in both Graves' disease and toxic MNG.
items.exp: T3/T4 ratio is < 15 in Subacute Thyroiditis, and > 20 in both Graves' Disease and Toxic MNG. (Book p916)

items.q: TSH-receptor stimulating antibodies are characteristically present in which of the three conditions?
opts: Both subacute thyroiditis and toxic MNG
items.exp: TSH-R stimulating Ab is Absent in Subacute Thyroiditis, Present in Graves' Disease, and Absent in Toxic MNG. (Book p916)

items.q: On ultrasound and color Doppler, what is described as the best test to diagnose Graves' disease on page 916?
opts: Diffusely enlarged gland with markedly increased vascularity (↑↑ vascularity)
Small shrunken gland with absent vascularity
Multiple hypoechoic nodules with peripheral flow
Thick calcified thyroid capsule with acoustic shadowing
items.exp: Ultrasound for Graves' Disease: 'Diffusely enlarged gland, ↑↑ vascularity (Best test to diagnose)'. (Book p916)

items.q: Match the radioiodine (RAI) uptake finding to the condition on page 916 — 1) Subacute Thyroiditis 2) Graves' Disease 3) Toxic MNG … A) Low uptake B) Markedly increased (↑↑) uptake C) Depends on functional status of nodules (cold or hot nodules)
items.exp: Radioiodine uptake: Subacute Thyroiditis = Low uptake; Graves' Disease = ↑↑ uptake; Toxic MNG = Depends on functional status of nodules (cold or hot nodules). (Book p916)

items.q: Which of the following features is NOT characteristic of Toxic Multinodular Goiter (MNG) in the page 916 table?
opts: Prominent infiltrative ophthalmopathy and pretibial dermopathy
Duration of symptoms spanning months to years
Commonly occurs in the elderly population (Females > Males)
Nodular goiter with enlarged nodules on ultrasound
items.exp: Ophthalmopathy and dermopathy are absent in toxic MNG; they are present only in Graves' disease. (Book p916)
